messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy started for prompt-routing-experiment -> prompt-router-v2 to prod (canary 10%)

sara: seeing spikes in error rate for /v2/prompt on the canary hosts — started ~2m after rollout

oncall-jen: got the page from incident-bot :rotating_light: paging now. @nate you're up next if I need a hand

incident-bot: Page sent to oncall-jen (sev: high) — symptom: 5xx spike, window: 15m, affected: hosted API prompt routing endpoints

oncall-jen: digging into logs, pulling list of canary instances and nginx logs

mike: traffic-shift trace shows X-Prompt-Variant: v2 header is present for older sessions and some clients. a few requests to prompt-router-v2 are returning 502s

sara: quick repro: run curl against canary router with a ~3k token prompt and it 502s consistently

oncall-jen: lowering canary weight to 0 while we triage, will flip feature flag if necessary

infra-luis: internal toggle endpoint available. command we use in ops: 
```
curl -X POST https://ff-admin.internal/api/flags/prompt-routing-experiment/toggle 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
 -d '{"enabled":false}'
```

oncall-jen: executing the toggle via admin UI (safe-mode): flipping "prompt-routing-experiment" -> OFF now

deploy-bot: Canary weight set to 0 for prompt-router-v2 by oncall-jen

sara: metrics: 5xx rate falling from ~12% to 0.8% within two minutes after toggle. P95 latency back to baseline

nate: taking over the page from jen — oncall handoff: @oncall-jen handing to @nate. I'll run follow-up mitigations and postmortem

nate: short mitigation: adding nginx header filter on edge to strip X-Prompt-Variant for clients that don't advertise streaming; rolling now

mike: rolling back the canary containers (image sha: abc123 -> previous stable) across the canary pool, started rollback job

prod-alex: customer impact note: support flagged 8 customers with degraded responses, 2 reported timeouts on prompts. No evidence of data loss or security impact. Some streaming sessions were truncated

oncall-jen: drafting status update to support & affected customers: 
"We deployed an experimental prompt routing change that caused errors for a subset of prompt sizes. We have disabled the experiment and rolled back canary instances. Services are stable and we are continuing verification. ETA for a full postmortem: 48 hours."

incident-bot: Incident declared: Sev2 at 1710456800 — automated page escalations triggered

sara: tagging root-cause candidates: flag toggle non-atomicity, v2 endpoint handshake mismatch on large prompts (tokenization/streaming), session affinity carrying outdated headers

nate: will own the postmortem. initial action items: (1) ensure flag toggles are immediate and atomic for routing flags, (2) add canary sanity check for prompt size handling, (3) add synthetic tests for streaming handshake backwards-compat

mike: note — observed tokenizer chunk boundary case where streaming state machine expected a preamble not provided by some clients; that caused the v2 handler to reject and 502 instead of graceful fallback

infra-luis: adding permanent guard: make the flag toggle run a preflight that checks active sessions and drains traffic before switching routing for stateful features

oncall-jen: marking page resolved after 20 minutes of stable metrics and customer notifications :white_check_mark:

sara: +1. schedule a short blameless retro Monday 10:30 and assign owners for fixes (infra-luis, sara, mike)

nate: created the postmortem doc and assigned to product/infra/eng-ml owners; will ping for reviews

deploy-bot: Deploys to prompt-router-v2 are paused until postmortem closes and fixes are in

prod-alex: customer comms sent to impacted customers. will follow up if any request for rollback credits or deeper remediation

incident-bot: incident cleared at 1710457045

oncall-jen: short follow-ups: add metric alert for sudden canary error deltas, make the FF toggle endpoint return operation-id and completion status, and document emergency kill-switch playbook in runbook repo

sara: thanks all. big win on the quick kill-switch toggle. we'll be more cautious with routing experiments that touch session affine headers."
